subject: Re: PoC deployment mode discussion — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC deployment mode follow-up — next steps

Hi Taylor,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet you and Priya. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we can align on the PoC approach.

Summary of needs you shared:
- Data residency and customer data controls are must-haves (security team expects VPC/KMS integration).
- Production target throughput ~200 req/s for text-generation (avg 300 tokens per request).
- Latency target: p99 < 200ms for 512-token responses.
- Initial PoC timeline: 4-6 weeks, with production goal in Q3 if successful.
- Stakeholders: Priya (security), Taylor (product), and infra (TBD).

Deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to spin up for feature-level validation, but requires gap analysis on VPC/KMS and SOC2 evidence.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool we can provision for predictable throughput; supports private network peering and custom autoscaling policies.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full network isolation and customer-managed control plane for regulated workloads (longer lead time).

Proposed PoC trial plan (options):
- Option A (Preferred for speed): Hosted API trial + VPN peering for test data, 4-week run. Success criteria: meet p99 latency target on representative load and basic KMS integration validated.
- Option B (If security requires): Short Dedicated trial — we provision a reserved pool with pre-configured VPC peering for 4 weeks. Success criteria: throughput and latency at scale + KMS integration.
- Option C (longer runway): Private deployment proof-of-concept; 6-8 weeks including infra onboarding.

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm which option you prefer (A/B/C).
- Introduce infra contact for peering and firewall rules.
- Share a representative prompt set + sample traffic profile (CSV or Playbook).

Action items from Redwood:
- Share PoC checklist and NDA (attached).
- Schedule short triage call with our infra engineer once infra contact is shared.
- Prepare a Dedicated capacity estimate if you prefer Option B.

Attached: PoC_Checklist_Acme_v1.pdf (checklist + success criteria template)

If you’re good with this approach I’ll get the paperwork started and loop in Dev for the peering/technical kickoff.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC deployment mode follow-up — next steps

Jordan - thanks for the clear recap. Priya and I reviewed internally and a few clarifications: 

1) Security: our security team will not accept a standard hosted SaaS connection without VPC peering + customer-managed keys. SOC2 evidence is required but not sufficient on its own.
2) Timeline: we want a 4-week technical PoC beginning mid-May. Production target still Q3.
3) Success criteria (engineering + security):
   - p99 latency < 200ms at 200 req/s for 512-token baseline
   - End-to-end encryption with our KMS for model inputs/outputs at rest and in transit
   - Ability to rollback to a smaller model variant if cost/latency needs require it

We are leaning toward Option B (Dedicated) assuming you can confirm the peering and KMS support. If Dedicated isn’t an option quickly, we can consider Option A with strict peering and a short-term workaround.

I’m copying Priya (security) - Priya, can you share who from infra should be our point of contact for firewall/VPN?

Thanks,
Taylor

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC deployment mode follow-up — next steps

Great - thanks, Taylor and Priya. We can support Option B (Dedicated) for the PoC and will validate KMS integration with your security team.

Next steps from Redwood: 
- I’ll get Dev (cc'd: Marissa and Ben) to scope the Dedicated pool sizing and share a cost/estimate within 48 hours.
- Dev (Marissa), can you confirm the minimal network/firewall rules needed for VPC peering and if we need any inbound access from Acme to our control plane?
- I’ve attached the signed NDA and the PoC checklist - please review and confirm.

Proposed PoC timeline:
- Week 0 (mid-May): network peering, KMS handshake, baseline infra checks
- Week 1: ingest representative prompt set; baseline latency tests
- Weeks 2-3: load testing at 200 req/s; iterate on batching/quant profiles
- Week 4: review, final acceptance against success criteria, and rollout planning

Can we schedule a 30-min technical kickoff for May 12th? Let me know a few slots that work for your infra team.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: PoC deployment mode follow-up — Acme Corp (internal kickoff)

(Forwarding the thread for technical scope)

Marissa / Dev - Acme is leaning to Dedicated capacity for a 4-week PoC starting mid-May. Key asks:
- Confirm Dedicated pool sizing to reach 200 req/s at p99 <200ms for 512 tokens (include model variant suggestions and quantization profile).
- Outline required network/firwall rules for VPC peering and KMS integration (we may need a short list for Acme infra).
- Provide a short runbook for measurement (what metrics we’ll capture, where).

Attaching PoC_Checklist_Acme_v1.pdf to share with the team.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PoC deployment mode follow-up — Acme Corp

Thanks - I’ll draft the Dedicated sizing and network checklist today. Initial notes:
- Recommended model: rwd-13b-q4 (or rwd-7b-q4 if cost needs force it) for latency balance.
- For 200 req/s with 512-token p99 target we should start with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs in the pool and enable aggressive batching with 20-40ms batch windows for small burst smoothing.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; need Acme key ARN and peering completed to validate key access.
- Metrics: token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates - capture via Console export link.

I’ll populate the PoC checklist with these items and share an internal runbook link.

Marissa
